data.hypothesis: Previous T3 measurements found the Horner-only rewrite correct at 0.007254 s, versus 0.007529 s for baseline; sqrtf(T) sharing alone measured 0.008214 s, and their combination measured 0.008066 s. This candidate leaves sqrtf expressions unchanged and uses a factored, balanced partial-sum evaluation of the same CND polynomial and coefficients. It tests whether the shorter dependency structure offsets its extra intermediate arithmetic; rounding and time remain for the controller to measure.

memory_lessons.applicability: Use these results as measured comparisons for further scalar CND and sqrtf(T) experiments, not as proof of the compiler's transformations.
memory_lessons.claim: The Horner-only rewrite passed the 8 varied correctness cases and measured 0.007254 s; sqrtf(T) sharing alone and Horner combined with that sharing also passed but measured 0.008214 s and 0.008066 s, respectively. The baseline measured 0.007529 s.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this distinct balanced polynomial evaluation against Horner-only for correctness, rounding, and time.

data.notes: This is an unmeasured, scalar-only CND evaluation-order experiment. The CND coefficients and mathematical polynomial are retained; the controller's varied-input correctness checks and timing determine whether the reassociation is acceptable and useful.
transformations: Rewrite only the supplied CND polynomial as a factored balanced partial-sum evaluation: compute k², the low pair, and the high group, then combine them. Retain all supplied coefficients and the surrounding CND formula.
Leave sqrtf(T), Black-Scholes option arithmetic, binomial code, and entrypoint unchanged.
